featured_reviews.name: Ravi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Nanumal Bhojraj (नानुमल भोजराज), 315, Shahid Bhagat Singh Rd, Ballard Estate, Fort, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400001 on 2nd September 2025 for lunch. I was in Colaba for a meeting and wasn’t sure where to eat, so I just searched “restaurants near me” and came across this place. Turns out it’s a very famous and old restaurant — and now I understand why!

What we ordered (3 people):

Paneer Tikka Masala
Butter Roti
Baingan Bharta with Bajre ki Roti
Chaas
Special Thali

The food was absolutely amazing — rich, flavourful, and very homely. The wait time was literally so less, which made the experience even better.

Seating options: They have two sections — ground floor (non-AC) and first floor (AC). Both looked comfortable, depending on what you prefer.

Ambience & Vibe: Classic, no-frills restaurant feel with quick service and hearty food. A perfect spot for family meals, groups, or even couples who enjoy traditional Indian cuisine.

Parking: Since it’s right on the main road, parking might be a bit tricky. Best to come walking if you’re nearby, or just take a taxi.

Overall: A gem of a place in Fort/Colaba — famous for a reason. Amazing food, quick service, and a legacy restaurant vibe. Highly recommended if you want authentic, satisfying vegetarian food in South Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Akhil Vaidya
featured_reviews.review_text: Gurukripa is a great spot in Sion offering a wide variety of snacks and sweets at affordable prices (around ₹200–₹300 per person). While everything is decent, their samosa truly stands out crispy, flavorful, and absolutely worth trying. It’s no surprise that Gurukripa is well-known for its samosas, which are widely supplied to cinemas and theatres across the city. Definitely recommended for a quick and tasty bite!

featured_reviews.name: Desii Thing
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would have easily given 5 stars, but recently the overall taste seems to have gone slightly down compared to what it used to be.

Still, the samosa with chutney and chole remains their signature and is absolutely worth trying — crisp, flavourful, and perfectly balanced. The gulab jamun is also soft, rich, and makes a great finish to the meal.

They have a wide variety of chaats, North Indian snacks, sweets, and quick bites — most items are decent in quality and value for money. Service is fast, and this place continues to be a popular local landmark with a loyal fan following over the years.

Only minor downsides are the slightly toned-down spice and taste recently, limited seating comfort, and parking challenges due to the busy area.

Overall, still one of the must-try classic spots in Mumbai for samosa-chole lovers — just wish they bring back their old flavour punch!

If you’re craving authentic North Indian flavors with a homely touch, Oye Kaka is a place you shouldn’t miss. The vibe is simple yet inviting, making it perfect for a relaxed meal with friends or family.
The highlight here is definitely the rich and flavorful gravies — their butter chicken and dal makhani stand out with just the right balance of spices and creaminess. The kebabs are well-cooked and juicy, adding a great start to the meal. Pair it all with soft, freshly made rotis or naan, and you’re sorted.
Portion sizes are generous, and the pricing feels reasonable for the quality served. Service is quick and friendly, though it can get a bit busy during peak hours.
Overall, Oye Kaka delivers comfort food that hits the spot — a solid choice when you’re in the mood for hearty Punjabi cuisine. Do order their Kulchas and karare bhendi as per pics..follow for for more reviews.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

Service: The service is consistently described as super fast, excellent, and the staff are noted as polite and friendly.
Atmosphere: The ambiance is casual and simple. It can get crowded, especially during office lunch hours (around 1:30 PM to 2:30 PM), and seating arrangements may be a bit uncomfortable during peak times.
Hygiene & Quality: The food is generally considered fresh, hygienic, and of good quality, often compared favorably to home-cooked meals.
Accessibility & Amenities: The establishment lacks wheelchair accessibility and does not have a public restroom.
Summary
Siddhivinayak Restaurant is a well-known spot in the Fort area, especially for local office workers, seeking a quick, satisfying, and inexpensive vegetarian meal. While it may not offer an upscale dining experience or extensive amenities, its core appeal lies in its delicious, budget-friendly food and efficient service.

One of the best culinary experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. I stumbled upon this spot tucked into one of the city’s busiest, most crowded streets, and it was absolutely worth navigating the chaos to get there.

I ordered the pav bhaji and chole bhature, and both were outstanding. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced with that authentic street-style flavor, yet it felt clean and hygienic. The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene

Most dishes were flavorful and well-prepared. The Puran Poli stood out – soft, perfectly sweet, and very satisfying. The Kothimbir Vadi was crispy and nicely spiced. The Seasonal Thali gave a good variety and felt wholesome.

featured_reviews.name: Sumit K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Aswad Restaurant is an excellent place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food in a clean, comfortable, and welcoming environment in dadar mumbai. The restaurant maintains very high standards of hygiene, which adds greatly to the overall dining experience.

The food is not only delicious but also very affordable, making it a great option for regular meals as well as for first-time visitors wanting to explore traditional Maharashtrian cuisine. Their **Maharashtrian thali** is highly recommended, offering a wholesome and satisfying combination of flavors. Special dishes like **Bhakri–Pithla** and **Thalipeeth** are prepared perfectly and taste truly homely.

One of the highlights of Aswad is their **Modak**, which is simply the best—fresh, flavorful, and a must-try for dessert lovers. The food is mild, not overly spicy or oily, making it suitable for all age groups and ideal for those who prefer healthy, home-style meals.

The service is polite, prompt, and courteous, adding to the pleasant atmosphere of the restaurant. Its convenient location near **Dadar Metro Station** makes it easily accessible in mumbai.

Overall, Aswad Restaurant is a wonderful choice for hygienic, affordable, and authentic Maharashtrian vegetarian food with a comforting, home-cooked feel. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Swad Stories
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Govinda's Restaurant near Chowpatty, Girgaon, and had a wonderful dining experience. What makes this place truly unique is that, being associated with the ISKCON Temple Trust, they do not use garlic or onions in any of their preparations. Despite this, the food is incredibly flavorful and satisfying, proving that great taste doesn't always need conventional ingredients.

The menu offers a wide variety of options across different cuisines. We started our meal with a selection of soups including Artichoke Bisque, Minestrone, Manchow, Tomato Lemongrass, and Laksa Soup. Each soup had a distinct flavor profile and was perfectly balanced. My personal favorite was the Artichoke Bisque Soup, as it was my first time trying it and I absolutely loved its rich, creamy texture and unique taste.

For starters, we ordered the Kung Pao Paneer and Masala Papad. The paneer was well-cooked with just the right amount of spice, while the masala papad made for a light and crunchy accompaniment.

In the main course, we enjoyed Paneer Lababdar and Dal Tadka paired with Jeera Rice. The gravies were comforting, flavorful, and complemented the rice beautifully.

The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the Sizzling Brownie. Served hot and indulgent, it was the perfect way to end the dining experience.

Overall, Govinda's is a small yet charming restaurant with a constant flow of patrons, which speaks volumes about its popularity. If you're looking for delicious vegetarian food with a unique sattvic approach, this place is definitely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Kiara Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
WAH 🚀! Just had an UNEXPECTEDLY EPIC meal at the Govinda's - didn't know food could vibe with divinity like this 🪔🍴!

🔹 *Jini Dosa*: Twisted, cheesy, and LOADED with fillings! It was like a party in my mouth 😮. The dosa was crispy, the cheese was melty... chef's touch 🧂!
🔹 *Benne Dosa*: Soft, buttery, South Indian heaven!. The benne (butter) was rich and aromatic - loved it!
🔹 *Farm Fresh Pizza*: Wait, a farm-fresh pizza inside a temple? 🤯! Toppings were fresh, crust was spot on 🍕. Got the vibe that the ingredients were picked fresh for the temple devotees... felt special!

Eating amidst the temple's vibes, felt like a foodie blessing 🙌. Service was super attentive 😊.

If you're around Iskon anywhere in the world, Govinda's is an absolute MUST 📍. Blend of divine vibes + tasty food = recipe for a soulful meal 👌."
